page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by 64 physical cores of the ARMv8-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor running at 2.6 GHz. It features 512.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance is equipped with 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a top-tier rating in the PassMark memory score and Geekbench multi-core tests, alongside a strong rating in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 6200.09 GB/sec and large block uncached read bandwidth at 253.52 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also demonstrate strong performance, processing 101.36 million operations per second in Redis.

While multi-threaded workloads like software compilation with Clang score in the top tier, single-core performance remains in the average tier. Additionally, text generation for small LLM models is rated as poor, though medium model text generation performs strongly. Given the high memory-to-core ratio, fast local NVMe storage, and strong database benchmarks, this server is suited for memory-intensive databases, caching layers, and high-throughput web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services r7gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server featuring 64 dedicated ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 physical cores running at 2.6 GHz, paired with 512.0 GB of RAM and 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core and memory performance, highlighted by strong memory bandwidth and high-throughput database operations, including 101.36 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core CPU performance and small-model LLM text generation are limited to average and poor tiers, respectively. This hardware profile makes the instance highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from local high-speed storage, such as relational databases, caching layers, software compilation, and static web serving.
